# go tool nm: a const map of at most 8 keys lowers to a switch lookup,
# so the binary holds no table symbol for it; a 9-key map lowers to a
# static perfect-hash table, and that table symbol sits in read-only data.
env GOPROXY=off
env GOTOOLCHAIN=local
mkdir $WORK/bin

cd main
logos build -o $WORK/bin/switchmap$GOEXE .
! stderr .
go tool nm $WORK/bin/switchmap$GOEXE
! stdout 'main\._logos_cm0_small_tab'
stdout ' R main\._logos_cm1_big_tab'
exec $WORK/bin/switchmap$GOEXE
stdout '^ok$'
cd ..

-- main/go.mod --
module example.com/switchmap

go 1.27

-- main/main.lgo --
package main

import "fmt"

const small = map[string]int{
	"s0": 0, "s1": 1, "s2": 2, "s3": 3, "s4": 4, "s5": 5, "s6": 6, "s7": 7,
}

const big = map[string]int{
	"b0": 0, "b1": 1, "b2": 2, "b3": 3, "b4": 4, "b5": 5, "b6": 6, "b7": 7, "b8": 8,
}

func main() {
	if (small["s1"] ?? -1) != 1 || (big["b1"] ?? -1) != 1 {
		fmt.Println("bad")
		return
	}
	fmt.Println("ok")
}
